meta.name: The Barnyard Co.

hours.note: CONFIRM — bio says 11 AM to 3 AM; a Nov 2025 post says 11 AM to 4 AM

meta.owner: CONFIRM — a customer comment names the owner as Harsh
meta.parking: Ample parking; repeatedly mentioned in reviews as a plus

voice.note: These are the cafe's own words, pulled from their own captions. Use them as the register to write in. Adapt — do not paste verbatim into headlines.
voice.coreIdea: Feel at home. Slow down. Stay a little longer.
recurringThemes: time slowing down; days softer, nights softer
comfort and calm rather than energy and buzz
community, gathering, and things made together
craft and care in how things are made
ownPhrasings: a place where days slow down and nights feel softer
where time slows, but work flows
more than just food — warmth, stories and a sense of belonging
a cafe should do more than serve, it should soothe

design.note: The architectural story. This is the strongest raw material on the site.
design.concept: Conceived as an unpretentious loft house — the inclusivity of a barnyard, built as a home rather than a restaurant, so regulars can make themselves at home.
materials: oxidised corten steel signage and doors
entry facade of upcycled bottles set into metal mesh
ceiling of pallet wood strips made from fruit-vendor crates collected at local farmers' markets
raw concrete floors; wooden flooring on the mezzanine
salvaged furniture sourced from Jogeshwari market, Mumbai
refurbished upholstery, Chesterfield couches, an Indian seating platform
ship lamps and vintage bakelite switches
vintage maps of Ahmedabad and work by regional artists
signatureObjects: A pair of vintage wardrobe doors mounted on the north wall as a single artwork.
An old Jogeshwari dining table, legs shortened to coffee-table height, its glass top enclosing vintage movie posters and a scatter of the coffee beans used in the cafe.

spaces.name: The facade
spaces.description: Oxidised corten steel signage and a wall of upcycled bottles set into metal mesh. The first thing you see, and the reason people stop.

spaces.name: The entry hall
spaces.description: A ceiling of pallet wood strips — fruit crates collected from local farmers' markets — running the length of the hallway, lined with salvaged objects and art before the room opens up.

spaces.name: The main floor
spaces.description: Exposed brick, raw concrete, black steel structure and floor-to-ceiling windows. The room the magazines photographed.

spaces.name: The mezzanine
spaces.description: Shared tables and a relaxed living area on wooden flooring, looking down over the main floor.

spaces.name: The courtyard
spaces.description: A central open-air court with varied seating, surrounded by planting.

spaces.name: The bowling alley
spaces.description: Recently opened. No further detail confirmed.
spaces.note: NO ASSETS ANYWHERE. Not on their Instagram, not on the web. Build the page, placehold the imagery, do not invent lane counts, pricing or hours.

spaces.name: The games corner
spaces.description: A pool table, board games and a shelf of books.

uses.name: Eat and drink
uses.note: Do not lead with this — see BRIEF.md section 4.

uses.name: Host something
uses.detail: Birthdays, ceremonies, private hire. The Architect's Diary explicitly describes the layout as flexible and multifunctional, hosting pop-ups and performances by night — useful third-party validation for this page.

uses.name: Shoot here
uses.detail: Film, photo, brand and influencer shoots. The strongest B2B argument: a ₹2-crore, 10,000 sq ft, magazine-published set that is already lit, dressed and varied across six distinct rooms.
uses.gap: Need a list of productions and brands that have actually shot here. Ask the owner.

uses.name: Bowl
uses.detail: The newest thing they have and completely unmarketed.

uses.name: Work late
uses.detail: Open until 3 AM, laptop-friendly, quiet corners. Their own co-working reel did 149,000 plays with nothing to convert it. Give this a section on /spaces, not its own page.

events.name: Coffee Garba
events.description: A Navratri evening of live folk music, coffee and food, run with iJam Artists & Events.

events.name: Hoodie Painting Workshop
events.description: A guided hands-on session turning a plain hoodie into a hand-painted piece. Materials provided, no experience needed, registration by form.
events.reach: 253,000 plays — the single highest-reach piece of content associated with the venue

events.name: Phone-free Sundays
events.description: A recurring series of phone-free afternoons — games, building things, conversation, no screens — run with Kaunversations.

events.name: NoCatch brand film
events.description: A brand shot their launch film on location at the cafe.
